en.title: Splits with Equal Distinct Character Counts
en.description:
Split the string into a non-empty prefix and a non-empty suffix, and count the split positions where both sides contain the same number of distinct characters.

The standard input/output format was compiled by CSWork; value ranges marked "this site" are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: A single line containing a lowercase string; on this site its length is 1..100000.
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: at all three cut points both sides contain only a, so the output is 3. Example 2: for b|ac and ba|c the two sides have different numbers of distinct characters, so the output is 0. Example 3: ab|aba and aba|ba both have two distinct characters on each side, so the output is 2.
hints: Start the right-side frequency counts from the whole string, move characters to the left side one by one, and maintain the number of distinct characters on both sides.
